'Average score in Math greater than 400' maps to AvgScrMath > 400 in satscores.

cases.sql_query: SELECT CDSCode FROM frpm WHERE "Enrollment (K-12)" + "Enrollment (Ages 5-17)" > 500 LIMIT 1000
assumptions: Total enrollment is defined as Enrollment (K-12) + Enrollment (Ages 5-17), per the provided evidence.
'Codes' refers to CDSCode, the school identifier in the frpm table.

cases.sql_query: SELECT MAX(f."Free Meal Count (Ages 5-17)" / f."Enrollment (Ages 5-17)") AS max_eligible_free_rate_5_17 FROM satscores AS s JOIN frpm AS f ON s.cds = f.CDSCode WHERE s.NumTstTakr > 0 AND (CAST(s.NumGE1500 AS REAL) / s.NumTstTakr) > 0.3 AND f."Enrollment (Ages 5-17)" > 0 LIMIT 1000
assumptions: Excellence rate is defined as NumGE1500 / NumTstTakr (per the provided evidence).
Eligible free rate for ages 5-17 is defined as Free Meal Count (Ages 5-17) / Enrollment (Ages 5-17) (per the provided evidence).
The filter 'over 0.3' is interpreted as strictly greater than 0.3.
Rows with NumTstTakr = 0 or Enrollment (Ages 5-17) = 0 are excluded to avoid division-by-zero.
The join is on satscores.cds = frpm.CDSCode.

cases.sql_query: SELECT RANK() OVER (ORDER BY s.AvgScrWrite DESC) AS rank, s.sname AS school_name, sch.CharterNum AS charter_number FROM satscores AS s JOIN schools AS sch ON s.cds = sch.CDSCode WHERE s.AvgScrWrite > 499 AND NOT sch.CharterNum IS NULL LIMIT 1000
assumptions: Rank is computed with RANK() (ties share the same rank) ordered by AvgScrWrite descending (highest scores get rank 1).
Per the evidence, a valid charter number is one that is NOT NULL, so only schools with non-null CharterNum are included.
The join between satscores and schools is on satscores.cds = schools.CDSCode.

cases.sql_query: SELECT f."School Name", s.Street, s.City, s.Zip, s.State FROM frpm AS f JOIN schools AS s ON f.CDSCode = s.CDSCode WHERE ABS(f."Enrollment (K-12)" - f."Enrollment (Ages 5-17)") > 30 LIMIT 1000
assumptions: Interpreted 'more than 30 difference' as the absolute difference (ABS) between Enrollment (K-12) and Enrollment (Ages 5-17) exceeding 30, since 'difference' in natural language implies magnitude.
Interpreted 'full street address' as the Street, City, Zip, and State columns from the schools table.
Used the evidence formula Enrollment (K-12) - Enrollment (Ages 5-17) as the basis for the difference calculation.

'10th and 11th schools with the highest enrollment' means ranking all rows in frpm by Enrollment (K-12) in descending order and selecting positions 10 and 11 (i.e., skipping the top 9).
Ties in Enrollment (K-12) are handled by SQLite's default (arbitrary) ordering among equal values; no secondary sort is specified.
The frpm table contains one row per school (CDSCode is the primary key), so each row represents a distinct school.

Grades 1-12 are represented by the K-12 columns in the frpm table (per provided evidence).
The eligible free or reduced price meal rate is computed as FRPM Count (K-12) / Enrollment (K-12).
Ties in FRPM Count (K-12) are broken arbitrarily by SQLite's default ordering when no secondary sort key is specified.
